chunks: And from him, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yusuf ibn al-Sukht, from Hamdan ibn al-Nadr, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn al-Sayqal, who said:

Abu al-Hasan, meaning al-Rida (peace be upon him), came out to us in Marw on the twenty-fifth of Dhu al-Qadah and said, 'Fast, for I have become a fasting person in the morning.' We said, 'May Allah be our ransom, which day is it?' He said, 'It is a day in which mercy was spread, the earth was spread out, the Ka'ba was erected, and Adam (peace be upon him) descended to it.'

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: Abu al-Hasan, a title for Imam Musa al-Kadhim and Imam Ali al-Rida
key_terms.الرِّضَا: Al-Rida, meaning 'the pleased one', a title for Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida
key_terms.الْكَعْبَةُ: The Ka'ba, the cube-shaped building in Mecca
key_terms.ذِي الْقَعْدَةِ: Dhu al-Qadah, the eleventh month of the Islamic lunar calendar

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of fasting on the 25th of Dhu al-Qadah according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) designates the 25th of Dhu al-Qadah as a day of voluntary fasting, linking it to the anniversary of Adam’s descent to earth. The Imam highlights the day’s spiritual significance by associating it with the manifestation of divine mercy, the establishment of the Ka'ba, and the beginning of human earthly life, thereby elevating it as a occasion for gratitude and reflection in Shia tradition.
